cases.name: design-deny-dquote-push-refspec
cases.why: An unbraced name followed by :r is a modifier even inside double quotes, so the refspec loses its first letter.

cases.name: design-deny-unquoted-show-path
cases.why: An unquoted $c followed by :c is the command-path modifier, here in the first stage of a pipeline.

cases.name: design-deny-dquote-uppercase-a
cases.why: Uppercase A is one of the three uppercase modifier letters, and the name sits mid-word inside double quotes.

cases.name: design-deny-for-loop-body
cases.command: for rev in a b; do git show $rev:crates/x.rs; done
cases.why: The modifier is inside a loop body, on the loop's own variable.

cases.name: design-list-cmdsub-uppercase-r
cases.why: Uppercase R is not among the letters zsh applies after an unbraced $name:, and the shell here leaves the text unchanged.

cases.name: design-deny-unquoted-heredoc-body
cases.why: zsh expands the body of a heredoc whose delimiter is unquoted, so a modifier there is applied.

cases.name: design-deny-positional-t
cases.why: A positional parameter takes a modifier the same way a name does.

cases.name: design-allow-braced-refspec
cases.why: Braces end the name before the colon, which is the rewrite the deny reason gives.

cases.name: design-allow-single-quoted
cases.why: Single quotes stop all expansion.

cases.name: design-allow-backslash-dollar
cases.why: A backslash before the dollar sign makes it literal, so no parameter is expanded.

cases.name: design-allow-quoted-heredoc-macro-fragment
cases.why: A Rust macro fragment in a heredoc with a quoted delimiter is never expanded; this is the near-miss D4 requires.

cases.name: design-allow-url-port
cases.why: A digit after the colon is not a modifier letter.

cases.name: design-allow-scp-slash
cases.why: A slash after the colon is not a modifier letter.

cases.name: design-allow-non-modifier-forms
cases.why: A second colon, a letter outside the list, and colons inside braces are none of them the unbraced modifier shape.

cases.name: design-allow-python-single-quoted
cases.why: Double quotes nested inside single quotes are ordinary characters, so zsh expands nothing in the Python source.

cases.name: author-deny-cmdsub-lowercase-path
cases.why: The command-substitution context of the design's README line, with a lowercase c after the colon so the modifier really applies.

cases.name: author-gating-bash-shell
cases.why: The same shape is silent when SHELL is /bin/bash, because the zsh rules apply only when SHELL's basename is zsh.

cases.name: author-gating-other-zsh-path
cases.why: A different path whose basename is zsh still enables the rule.

cases.name: author-gating-empty-shell
cases.why: An empty SHELL has no zsh basename, so the rule stays silent.

cases.name: author-deny-g-then-s
cases.why: g followed by s is the global substitution modifier.

cases.name: author-deny-g-then-ampersand-dquote
cases.why: Inside double quotes g followed by & is the global repeat-substitution modifier.

cases.name: author-unquoted-g-then-background
cases.why: Measured on this host: an unquoted & is the background operator and ends the word, so zsh prints :g unchanged and applies no modifier.

cases.name: author-allow-g-then-other
cases.why: g followed by anything but s or & is not a modifier.

cases.name: author-deny-host-path-t
cases.why: t after the colon is the tail modifier, so a host:path without a leading slash is rewritten.

cases.name: author-deny-user-colon-s
cases.why: s after the colon starts a substitution, which zsh rejects as a bad substitution.

cases.name: author-deny-assignment-value
cases.why: An assignment value is expanded, so the modifier applies there too.

cases.name: author-deny-hash-mid-word
cases.why: A # inside a word does not start a comment, so the expansion after it is live.

cases.name: author-allow-comment
cases.why: A # at the start of a word begins a comment, which is never expanded.

cases.name: author-allow-quote-before-colon
cases.why: The closing quote sits between the name and the colon, so no modifier is read.

cases.name: author-allow-backslash-colon
cases.why: A backslash before the colon makes it literal, so the name ends without a modifier.

cases.name: author-deny-single-inside-double
cases.why: Single quotes inside double quotes are ordinary characters and do not stop expansion.

cases.name: author-allow-double-inside-single
cases.why: Double quotes inside single quotes are ordinary characters, and the single quotes stop expansion.

cases.name: author-deny-bash-c-double-quoted
cases.why: zsh expands a double-quoted argument before bash receives it, so handing it to another shell does not protect it.

cases.name: author-allow-ansi-c-quoted
cases.why: ANSI-C quoting expands no parameters.

cases.name: author-deny-backticks
cases.why: A backtick body is expanded like a command substitution.

cases.name: author-deny-dash-heredoc
cases.why: The <<- form strips leading tabs and still expands its body when the delimiter is unquoted.

cases.name: author-allow-double-quoted-delimiter
cases.why: A double-quoted delimiter disables expansion of the heredoc body.

cases.name: author-allow-backslash-delimiter
cases.why: A backslash-quoted delimiter disables expansion of the heredoc body.

cases.name: author-allow-partly-quoted-delimiter
cases.why: Quoting any part of the delimiter disables expansion of the whole body.

cases.name: author-allow-escaped-in-unquoted-heredoc
cases.why: A backslash before the dollar sign keeps it literal inside an unquoted heredoc body.

cases.name: author-deny-single-quotes-in-unquoted-heredoc
cases.why: Single quotes in an unquoted heredoc body are literal characters and do not stop expansion.

cases.name: author-deny-cmdsub-in-unquoted-heredoc
cases.why: A command substitution in an unquoted heredoc body runs, and its words are expanded.

cases.name: author-allow-special-parameter
cases.why: The rule names only a NAME or a digit, so a special parameter is outside it even though zsh would apply the modifier.

cases.name: author-deny-name-with-underscore-digit
cases.why: A name containing an underscore and a digit is one name, so the colon follows it directly.

cases.name: author-deny-uppercase-p
cases.why: Uppercase P is in the list, so a path beginning with P is resolved as a real path.

cases.name: author-allow-uppercase-outside-list
cases.why: Uppercase letters other than A, P and Q are not modifiers.

cases.name: author-allow-colon-at-end
cases.why: A colon with nothing after it is not a modifier.

cases.name: author-deny-parameter-zero
cases.why: Positional parameter 0 takes the head modifier like any other digit.
